title: Tree-Shaking & Code Splitting

subtopics.title: Static imports
subtopics.explanation: Build tools can follow static import and export statements to see which parts of a package are used. Dynamic runtime patterns may make that analysis harder.

subtopics.title: Unused exports
subtopics.explanation: Tree-shaking removes code that analysis shows is unused. Packages must expose modules in a way the tool can analyze, and some files have side effects that must remain.

subtopics.title: Code splitting
subtopics.explanation: Code splitting puts separate parts of an app into files that can load at different times. A route’s code can wait until someone visits that route.

subtopics.title: Lazy loading
subtopics.explanation: Lazy loading delays noncritical code until a user needs it, often through a dynamic import or route boundary. Show a useful loading state while the chunk arrives. Do not split every tiny helper into a separate request; too many chunks add network overhead and complexity.

subtopics.title: Verify the result
subtopics.explanation: A bundle analyzer shows what code was emitted, and browser network tools show what a page actually downloads. Compare the same routes before and after a change using production builds. Confirm that a smaller bundle did not introduce missing features, extra requests, or a slower first interaction.

foundations.overview: Builds can remove provably unused code and load some features only when needed.
foundations.whyItMatters: These ideas affect how quickly, reliably, and safely a frontend works.
foundations.browserPerspective: The bundler analyzes imports before the browser downloads the resulting chunks.
foundations.realWorldUsage: Use tree-shaking for unused exports and route splitting for work needed later.
foundations.businessImpact: Smaller initial downloads can help users on slow connections.
foundations.engineeringImpact: Avoid dynamic imports that obscure dependencies without a clear benefit.
foundations.performanceImpact: Measure transfer size, parse time, execution time, and request count.

commonMisconceptions.reality: Side effects and module formats can prevent safe removal.
Too many small requests and duplicated dependencies can slow a page.
